requirements.evidence: All contract routes present with correct names/middleware (routes/web.php:19-38: guest group, throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed on verification.verify, auth+verified on home). Login rate-limits per lowercased e-mail+IP with 5 tries and auth.throttle/auth.failed on `email` (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:23-46), regenerates session and redirectIntended to home (:50-52). Register uses the exact `str()->transliterate('register|'.$ip)` key (Register.php:27), Password::defaults() configured once (AppServiceProvider.php:24-26), fires Registered, logs in, regenerates. Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (NewPasswordController.php:33-38); single email input in reset view. EmailVerificationRequest gives 403 on tampered id; resend skips verified users (EmailVerificationController.php:39-41). .env.example and phpunit.xml locale pins done; ui.php in both locales. Gaps: Login validates with the `lowercase` rule (Login.php:35), so a correctly-cased-but-uppercase e-mail is rejected instead of normalised; no tests to show the requirements actually pass.

conventions.evidence: Conventions demand test-first and 'everything implemented ships with a test' — the diff contains zero test files. Livewire components validate with inline arrays in `$this->validate([...])` (Login.php:34-38, Register.php:39-43) instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attribute pattern. User creation done directly with User::create in the component (Register.php:45) rather than an Action. Positives: CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased], route() used everywhere, controllers use inline $request->validate, Bulma markup.

security.evidence: Login/register rate-limited inside the method; session regenerated after login; logout invalidates and regenerates token (LogoutController.php:13-17); forgot-password ignores sendResetLink status so it does not reveal existence (PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-26); EmailVerificationRequest authorizes id/hash; remember_token rotated on reset; all output via {{ }}; User keeps #[Fillable(['name','email','password'])]. Minor: Register clears the IP limiter on success (Register.php:55), so one IP can register unlimited accounts as long as each succeeds, which weakens the per-IP limit.

tests.evidence: No tests/ files in change.diff at all: nothing for login/register (incl. throttle, unauthorized/tamper cases required by the Livewire policy), logout, home redirects, password reset, verification tamper 403, or locale rendering, despite phpunit.xml being edited.

simplicity.evidence: Controllers are short and lean on framework features (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, RateLimiter). Some duplication: the throttle block is copy-pasted in Login and Register; the hasVerifiedEmail check in verify() (EmailVerificationController.php:26) is redundant with the final redirect; layout supports both $slot and @yield; translation key `color_code` => '#3273dc' duplicated in both locales is pointless.

readability.evidence: PHP classes are clear and well named. All Blade views are written with no indentation at all (e.g. resources/views/livewire/auth/register.blade.php, layouts/app.blade.php), and the existing indented welcome/bulma-test views were flattened, making nested Bulma markup hard to follow and inconsistent with the original sibling style. Repeated section/container/columns wrapper markup not extracted into a Blade component.

scope.evidence: Converting welcome.blade.php and bulma-test.blade.php to translations is requested by the task ('never hardcoded', applies to existing views). Small unrelated edits: dropped the `@fonts` directive from welcome (now not in layout), rewrote both pages onto the new layout with an auth navbar, and turned a colour hex into a translation key.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, violating the mandatory TDD convention and the Livewire definition of done (happy path, validation failure, unauthorized and tamper tests).
Livewire components validate with inline rule arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] property attributes.
The `lowercase` rule rejects e-mails typed with uppercase letters on login instead of normalising them, so valid users can fail to log in.
Clearing the per-IP register limiter after each successful registration lets one IP create accounts without limit.
User creation is written directly in the component rather than through an app/Actions class as the conventions require for writes.
All new and rewritten Blade views have no indentation, and repeated wrapper markup is not extracted into a Blade component.
The existing `@fonts` directive was dropped when moving welcome onto the new layout.
A colour hex code ('color_code' => '#3273dc') is stored as a translation key, which is not translatable text.
The early hasVerifiedEmail redirect in verify() is redundant since markEmailAsVerified is idempotent and the method redirects home anyway.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, password reset, e-mail verification, pt_BR/en ui translations, locale pins) with mostly correct and secure framework usage. However it ships no tests whatsoever, which the project's TDD and Livewire security policy make mandatory, and it bypasses the #[Validate] convention, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
